atoms.text: A clef must be included in the stave.
A clef specifies which pitch a note on the note lines corresponds to.

atoms.title: What do you need the clef for?

atoms.text: You have already learnt that when notes are particularly low they are written under the stave using ledger lines.
When you want to indicate very low notes, it becomes more and more difficult to read these using ledger lines. In this situation, you would use a different clef to specify a lower pitch.
The same notes can be written in different clefs, and look like this for example:
The notes in the second stave have a much higher position than those in the first.
This means that in this example, these notes indicate different pitches, even though they are in the same position on the stave.

instruction.text: Select each note, starting with the note in the treble clef.

atoms.text: As you can hear, the note in the treble clef (above) is higher than the note in the bass clef (below) even though both notes are in the same position on the stave.
atoms.sound: As you can hear, the note in the treble clef is higher than the note in the bass clef even though both notes are in the same position on the stave.

atoms.text: Which clef is used depends on the pitch of the piece of music, as well as which instrument it is written for.
The most common clefs are the treble clef, which specifies a higher pitch, and the bass clef, which specifies a lower pitch.
The treble clef is one of the most well-known clefs.
atoms.sound: The treble clef is one of the most well-known clefs.

atoms.text: The bass clef is also used frequently. It refers to a lower pitch than the treble clef.
atoms.sound: The bass clef is also used frequently. It refers to a lower pitch than the treble clef.

atoms.text: There are also more clefs in addition to the treble and bass clefs.
This, for example, is the alto clef.
atoms.sound: This, for example, is the alto clef.

instruction.text: Drag and match the correct pictures and descriptions.

atoms.text: There are often several clefs used in one piece of music. This especially makes sense if many instruments are playing together, for example in an orchestra.
atoms.sound: There are often several clefs used in one piece of music. This especially makes sense if many instruments are playing together, for example in an orchestra.

atoms.text: With certain instruments, such as the piano, two clefs are played at the same time: the right hand plays notes on the treble clef, and the left hand plays the notes on the bass clef.
atoms.sound: With certain instruments, such as the piano, two clefs are played at the same time: the right hand plays notes on the treble clef, and the left hand plays the notes on the bass clef.

atoms.b: Using the lines we can compare which notes are higher or lower. The clef further indicates the pitch of a ((--letter ++note)) and the ((++pitch duration)) of the stave itself. The most well-known clefs are the ((++treble trouble tribble)) and ((bass boss bus)) clefs.
There are additional clefs, for example the ((++alto balto)) clef.
In one piece of music, you can use ((no ++various)) clefs.
